front: Name the three tricuspid valve leaflets and their relative sizes.
Tricuspid annular dilation is present at an end-diastolic diameter > {{c1::40 mm (or 21 mm/m²)}}.
State three quantitative criteria for SEVERE tricuspid regurgitation.
back: Vena contracta ≥ 0.7 cm, EROA ≥ 0.40 cm², regurgitant volume ≥ 45 mL/beat. Also: systolic hepatic vein flow reversal, dense triangular early-peaking CW envelope.

front: What hepatic vein finding indicates severe TR?
back: Systolic hepatic vein flow reversal. (Normal HV Doppler shows a dominant S wave forward.)

front: How is pulmonary artery systolic pressure estimated from a TR jet?
back: PASP = 4·(TR peak velocity)² + right atrial pressure. RA pressure is estimated from IVC size and inspiratory collapsibility.

front: Give the RA pressure estimation categories based on IVC size and collapsibility.
back: Normal RA (~3 mmHg): IVC ≤ 2.1 cm AND > 50% collapse with sniff. Elevated (~15 mmHg): IVC > 2.1 cm AND < 50% collapse. Intermediate (~8 mmHg): one criterion but not both.

front: How do you estimate MEAN pulmonary artery pressure from a PR jet?
back: Mean PAP ≈ 4·(early diastolic PR peak velocity)².

front: How do you estimate PA end-diastolic pressure from a PR jet?
back: PA end-diastolic pressure ≈ 4·(end-diastolic PR velocity)² + right atrial pressure.

front: How does carcinoid heart disease typically affect the tricuspid valve?
back: Thickened, retracted, immobile leaflets → mixed tricuspid regurgitation and stenosis. The pulmonic valve is similarly affected. Left-sided involvement only occurs if there is right-to-left shunting (PFO) or bronchial carcinoid.

front: Two most common causes of secondary (functional) tricuspid regurgitation?
back: Right ventricular / right atrial enlargement from pulmonary hypertension, and long-standing atrial fibrillation with annular dilation.

front: When should tricuspid annuloplasty be considered at the time of left-sided valve surgery even without severe TR?
back: When the tricuspid annulus is dilated (> 40 mm) even with mild-moderate TR, since untreated annular dilation predicts future TR progression.

front: Which leaflet of the TV is most often involved in IE from a VSD, and why?
back: Septal leaflet — its close anatomic proximity to the membranous VSD jet exposes it to bacterial deposition.
